name: Livestock Water Requirement Calculator
seoTitle: Livestock Water Requirement Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Water intake scales with dry-matter intake and with heat, and it is the number most often under-designed on a farm. Free livestock water requirement calculato
summary:
Water intake scales with dry-matter intake and with heat, and it is the number most often under-designed on a farm. It returns water per animal per day, herd water per day, herd water per week and peak flow for a 4-hour drinking window, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator estimates daily and weekly water demand for a herd from body weight, species and temperature, together with the peak flow rate a trough has to deliver. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Livestock Water Requirement
sections.html:
Daily water (L/animal) = body weight × species factor × temperature correction; temperature correction = 1 + 0.02 × (temp − 20 °C) above 20 °C

The symbols in the formula

sections.title: How do I use the Livestock Water Requirement?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: species set to 1.0, average body weight of 500 kg, ambient temperature of 25°C.

Substituting them into the formula gives water per animal per day of 55 L, herd water per day of 1,100 L, herd water per week of 7,700 L, peak flow for a 4-hour drinking window of 275 L/h, number of animals of 20.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
cattle0.10 L/kgroughly 50 L for a 500 kg cow at 20 °C
sheep / goat0.08–0.09 L/kg4–6 L for a 50 kg ewe
pig0.12 L/kgabout 18 L for a 150 kg sow
poultry0.20 L/kgapproximately 0.3 L per hen per day

  • Intake climbs steeply with heat: a 500 kg cow needs about 50 L at 20 °C and around 70 L at 40 °C, which is why summer failures are usually a flow problem rather than a volume one.

  • Lactation adds 30–50% for dairy cattle; the calculator deliberately gives the maintenance figure and says so.

  • Peak flow matters: animals drink most of their water in a few hours after milking or feeding, so a trough sized for the daily total can still leave the herd waiting.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Sizing storage for the daily total but not the trough's refill rate.
  • Ignoring the temperature term in summer, which is where most shortfalls appear.
  • Using mature weight for growing animals, which overstates demand.

faq.q: How much water does a cow drink a day?
faq.a: About 40–70 litres for a 500 kg beef cow at moderate temperatures, rising to 100 litres or more in heat or during lactation.

faq.q: How do I size a trough?
faq.a: Give the herd its daily requirement in one to two hours of refill, which is what the peak flow figure here approximates.

faq.q: What does the Livestock Water Requirement actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns water per animal per day, herd water per day, herd water per week and peak flow for a 4-hour drinking window. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
